item.text:
**5B.7 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Bottom line:** *Mixed, leaning evidence-based rather than slogan-only.* The clearest 2024 pattern is reactive correction in food/inflation policy, plus technocratic, rule-based reforms in procurement and investment. The main counterweight is that the rice agenda stayed heavily campaign-framed and politically visible, with some self-congratulatory official messaging and criticism that fixes could favor importers.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Marcos economic team lays out plans to safeguard PH economy` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-07-08 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228524) | Marcos’s economic managers publicly laid out macro strategy in a forum with NEDA, BSP, DBM, Treasury, and the presidential investment office. This is strong evidence of technocratic, evidence-informed policy management rather than pure slogan politics. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.6` |
| `Marcos urges Congress to allow NFA to import rice` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-05-25 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1225525) | Marcos backed changing rice-import rules to stabilize prices, showing willingness to alter policy in response to inflation pressure instead of defending the status quo. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6` |
| `Economist: Rice tariff cut to ease inflation` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-12 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1226754) | The tariff cut was justified with an inflation estimate and approved by the NEDA Board chaired by Marcos, which is direct evidence of data-based policy correction. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `PBBM expects rice prices to ease further` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-24 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-expects-rice-prices-to-ease-further/) | Marcos explicitly tied rice-price expectations to observed regional trends and a sectoral inflation meeting, showing he was tracking price data and projecting adjustment rather than denying the problem. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3` |
| `New law to make procurement ‘at par with global best practices’: PBBM` | Philippine News Agency | 2024-07-22 | [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1229520) | Procurement reform was framed as modernization and efficiency, not patronage. This supports a reading of rule-based administration and cleaner public contracting. | `5B.7`; also `5B.5`, `5B.6` |
| `PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | The government standardized forms and institutionalized e-procurement, which cuts room for favoritism and discretionary extraction. | `5B.7`; also `5B.5`, `5B.6` |
| `Philippines' Marcos signs tax reform law to lure foreign investment` | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-11-10 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/philippines-marcos-signs-tax-reform-law-to-lure-foreign-investment-3713493) | CREATE MORE lowered corporate taxes and expanded incentives, showing structural pro-investment reform rather than purely rhetorical management. It is also selective, so not pure neutrality. | `5B.7`; also `5B.4`, `5B.6` |
| `PBBM’s economic reforms improved lives in 2024` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-12-31 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbms-economic-reforms-improved-lives-in-2024/) | The administration’s year-end wrapup claims liberalization, privatization, globalization, and inflation management. Useful as self-positioning, but weaker than independent evidence. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `$0.343/kilo rice still possible - Department of Agriculture, Philippines` | Reuters via Zawya | 2024-07-24 | [link](https://www.zawya.com/en/markets/commodities/0343-kilo-rice-still-possible-department-of-agriculture-philippines-vwstcm9g) | Reuters notes the cheap-rice target was a campaign promise, showing that rice policy remained politically marketed and popularity-sensitive. This is the clearest evidence for slogan-driven pressure. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |
| `Imports unlikely to cut rice prices` | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-07-09 | [link](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/07/09/607056/imports-unlikely-to-cut-rice-prices/) | Critics argued the tariff/import approach could favor importers and hurt farmers, suggesting a politically visible fix with distortion risk rather than clean evidence-led reform. | `5B.7`; also `5B.3`, `5B.4` |

| `PBBM ushers Filipinos to a Bagong Pilipinas that serves its people` | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-01-28 | [link](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-bagong-pilipinas-that-serves-its-people/) | The opening 2024 frame was branding-heavy. It signals slogan-based governance messaging, but not by itself policy denial or correction. | `5B.7` |

**Synthesis**
- Best evidence for `5B.7` is the inflation/rice sequence: the administration acknowledged the pain point, changed tariffs, pushed NFA import flexibility, and later cited observed price trends.
- Best evidence against is the persistent `P20 rice` campaign framing and the risk that the chosen fix could favor importers and create distortions.
- On balance, Marcos in 2024 looks more like a ruler making reactive, data-anchored adjustments under pressure than one governing mainly by denial or scapegoating.
- I did not find strong independent evidence of a formal “mistake admission” culture outside rice/inflation, so the correction pattern is real but narrow.

**Search gap**
- Reliable 2024 evidence is thin on a documented cross-sector correction process. Most clear examples of learning-from-data are concentrated in food prices, tariffs, procurement, and investment rules.
